chunks: And the report narrated by Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man's sleep while sitting [invalidate wudu]?' He said: 'My father used to say: If a man sleeps while sitting in a composed manner, wudu is not required of him; but if he sleeps lying down, wudu is required of him.'

Likewise, all the other narrations that have come down denying the renewal of wudu on account of sleep — for they are many — their meaning is that [wudu is not invalidated] if [the sleep] does not overcome the intellect and the person remains composed and in control of what proceeds from him.

key_terms.الْعَقْلِ: the intellect, rational faculty (jurisprudential criterion for wudu invalidation)

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping while sitting in a composed position invalidate wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Bakr ibn Abi Bakr al-Hadrami from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), records a ruling attributed to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS): sleeping while sitting in a composed, upright position does not require wudu, whereas sleeping while lying down does. Shaykh al-Tusi appends an explanatory note that the many narrations denying the obligation of wudu after sleep apply specifically to light sleep that does not overcome a person's rational faculty and self-control.
